text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A states a clear position on driverless cars and defends it throughout, while Essay B mostly summarizes the article without taking a stance", "quality": "Clear position and argumentative stance", "description": "The essay commits to a position on driverless cars and sustains that argument rather than merely retelling article content."}, {"evidence": "Essay A addresses the liability question ('whos is to blame') and proposes a solution with speed limits, while Essay B never engages counterarguments", "quality": "Counterargument handling", "description": "The essay anticipates and responds to an objection to its position, strengthening the overall argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay A uses article details (BMW Traffic Jam Assistant, LIDAR, 3-D modeling, 25 mph limit) as evidence to support its claims about safety", "quality": "Purposeful evidence use", "description": "The essay selects and deploys source details in service of its own claims rather than listing facts without connecting them to an argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay A has an introduction, body paragraphs developing distinct points, and a conclusion that returns to the thesis", "quality": "Organized essay structure", "description": "The essay is arranged into recognizable introduction, body, and conclusion sections that build the argument coherently."}, {"evidence": "Essay A reasons that combining computer and human eyes on the road would reduce accidents caused by human error like drinking or texting", "quality": "Causal reasoning", "description": "The essay explains why driverless cars would improve safety by drawing logical connections between causes and effects."}, {"evidence": "Essay A concludes with a forward-looking reflection on growth and the future, tying back to its thesis", "quality": "Coherent conclusion", "description": "The essay closes by reinforcing its central claim rather than trailing off or introducing unrelated content."}]}
